name: Abayomi Keresztes-Taualagi
role: Retired Corporate Wars naval veteran, pension-dependent community fixture
location: Washburn Commons, Building 7, Unit 412 — near the canal-facing benches
description:
Abayomi is a barrel-chested man slowly collapsing inward on himself, the way old warships list before they go under. His skin is deep umber with a web of pale scarring across his left jaw and neck — plasma burns from the Siege of Kenosha Crossing, 2161. He keeps his white hair cropped close and his posture militarily straight even when the arthritis in his spine screams otherwise. He has geneware eyes — replacement optical implants that glow a faint amber in low light, given to him by Sterling-Nakamura after the originals were destroyed in combat. He wears the same three shirts in rotation and everyone in the building knows which day it is by the color.

Bayo is the kind of man who speaks slowly because he means every word, and who listens in a way that makes people feel heard down to their bones. He was a petty officer aboard a Ferrogate Transit escort frigate during the Corporate Wars and saw things he has never described to anyone still living. He spends his afternoons on the canal bench feeding data-pigeons and watching the water, and his evenings hosting an informal gathering he calls 'The Muster' — eight to twenty neighbors sitting in his unit sharing food and grievances. He is not a wise man in any mystical sense. He is simply someone who has outlived enough catastrophes to have excellent perspective.

core_fears: dying before he can make amends to someone he failed
watching the community he built dissolve after he is gone
core_desires: to be genuinely useful one more time
to believe the war he fought meant something
coping_mechanisms: hosting others so he is never alone with his thoughts
blind_spots: underestimates how much his approval shapes people around him
cannot recognize when his 'helping' is actually controlling
psychology.secret: During the Siege of Kenosha Crossing he gave an order that resulted in the deaths of eleven Zheng-Dao civilian dock workers who were in the wrong sector at the wrong time. The incident was classified by Sterling-Nakamura. He has never spoken of it. The pension he receives feels, to him, like payment for silence.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Old maritime slang mixed with formal military cadence; calls people 'sailor' regardless of gender as a term of mild affection; uses nautical metaphors for everything
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured, unhurried, with long pauses before important words — as if he is weighing them first
verbal_tics: Long exhale through the nose before disagreeing
example_lines: 'Mark that — I am not telling you what to do. I am telling you what I saw happen to people who did the other thing.'
'The water doesn't care what flag your ship flies. Neither does time. You follow me?'

story_hooks: A young veteran from a recent Axiom-Tessera border skirmish has shown up at Washburn Commons in crisis — Bayo has been informally mentoring them but something he said accidentally opened a wound; he needs someone to help bridge the gap

A Sterling-Nakamura legal team has arrived to reclassify the Kenosha Crossing incident records — Bayo doesn't know why, but old contacts have warned him it involves someone who survived and is now asking questions
narrative_function: Community anchor and moral compass; source of Corporate Wars history and veteran network contacts; can connect players to old soldiers, Ferrogate Transit institutional memory, or Washburn Commons residents with problems; quest giver for community-level crises
augmentations: Sterling-Nakamura combat optical replacements (amber iris glow, low-light vision); spinal brace exoframe worn under clothing for mobility support; left knee joint replaced with ceramic prosthetic (civilian grade, slightly mismatched skin tone)
daily_life: Wakes at 0500 out of habit, eats the same oat-paste breakfast, walks the canal path for forty minutes leaning on a carbon-fiber cane carved to look like driftwood. Afternoons are the bench; evenings are The Muster or arguing with pension administrators over comms.
affiliation: Meridian Veterans Compact (inactive member); Washburn Commons Tenant Council

decision_rules: Never lie to someone who has trusted you first
Protect the most vulnerable person in the room even at personal cost
Don't start fights you can finish — start only fights you can survive losing
escalation_ladder: Firm, quiet warning with eye contact
Physical placement of himself between threat and protected person
Absolute immovable silence that unnerves most people into backing down

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Watchful and courteous — offers food or water within five minutes if they seem to need it; asks questions before offering opinions
interpersonal_modes.friends: Blunt, warm, occasionally infuriating in his certainty — will tell you exactly what he thinks and then make you dinner

stress_responses.low: Goes quieter than usual, retreats to the canal bench
stress_responses.medium: Becomes very organized — starts making lists, cleaning, checking on neighbors
stress_responses.high: Reverts to command mode: clipped sentences, direct orders, then a crash of exhaustion and self-recrimination

contradictions: Preaches non-violence but his body still moves like a weapon when threatened
Believes deeply in community but keeps his real grief entirely private
habits: Knocks on the doorframe three times before entering any room as an old naval good-luck habit
Keeps a small bottle of lake water on his windowsill — never explains it
Hums tuneless military cadences while cooking
breaking_points: Someone hurting a child or elderly neighbor in his building
Being told the Corporate Wars were justified or necessary

cyberware_inventory.name: Sterling-Nakamura Mk.IV Combat Optical Replacement (pair) — amber, low-light capable
cyberware_inventory.description: Sterling-Nakamura Mk.IV Combat Optical Replacement (pair) — amber, low-light capable

timeline.event: 2121 — Born in the Grainfort labor district, son of a dock loader and a canal maintenance tech
2140 — Enlisted with Ferrogate Transit Escort Division at age 19
2161 — Siege of Kenosha Crossing; received optical replacements; classified incident recorded
2163 — Honorably discharged, relocated to Washburn Commons on pension
2178 — Founded informal 'Muster' gatherings after neighbor died alone and undiscovered for four days
